I'm also checking that the taxpayer isn't a nonresident alien, and whether a person who is a dependent only under 152(d)(2)(H) should be excluded.

I'm deciding whether the dependent-only-under-152(d)(2)(H) exclusion should apply to every person in the head of household test or only to the dependent branch. Applying it to everyone would force unnecessary reviews when a father or mother's status is unknown, so I'm leaning toward limiting it to the dependent path.

I'm deciding to apply the 152(d)(2)(H) exclusion only to the dependent branch of the head of household test, since a qualifying child can't be a dependent only by that route and a father or mother isn't affected by it either. That keeps the check from forcing reviews on the other branch.

I'm checking the head of household section's references to 3.1 through 5.4, and I want each one cited by a quoted sentence. I'm also making sure the 152(d)(2)(H) exclusion stays on the dependent branch only, and that the married-at-close test still uses the spouse's nonresident-alien status.

I'm weighing whether to split the head of household rule into separate disjunctive rules, one per not-married route, so each can cite its own sections. I'm splitting the head of household rule into four separate rules by not-married route: unmarried at the determination date, separated, a nonresident-alien spouse, and living apart. Each one cites its own sections, and the spouse-death condition gets cited in the rules where it applies.

I'm settling on the head of household rule as one rule rather than splitting it by route, and noting that the spouse-death override against the separation exception has to be resolved one way or the other.

I'm checking the remaining head of household conditions against the rules: the principal-abode test is covered by the whole-year check, the father or mother branch by the existing person fields, and the child test by the child relationship field. I'm also noting that the "not married at close of year" requirement is handled by the determination-date check, and that "not a surviving spouse" is already settled by the outcome order.

Working out the surviving spouse rule's conditions: the spouse died within the two preceding years, and the taxpayer doesn't have a spouse who was a nonresident alien during the year. I'm now setting up the head of household maintenance test for each person.

I'm settling the surviving spouse rule's conditions, and checking the deemed-married exception for a spouse who died during the year: a divorced taxpayer's former spouse dying wouldn't make them married, so I'm weighing whether the death-year test needs a marriage check alongside it.

Writing the furnished-home branch of the head of household rule as code now...

Still writing the head of household rule's furnished-home conditions...

Then I'm moving on to the surviving spouse definition in 2.1, which requires the spouse to have died within the two preceding years and the taxpayer to maintain a home for a dependent.

request.messages: the prompt below, as the one user message

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be decided on it.

persons.text: For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer- (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151. ... An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either- (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of- (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child- (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151.

rules.text: For purposes of section 1, the term "surviving spouse" means a taxpayer- (A) whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year, and (B) who maintains as his home a household which constitutes for the taxable year the principal place of abode (as a member of such household) of a dependent (i) who (within the meaning of section 152) is a son, stepson, daughter, or stepdaughter of the taxpayer, and (ii) with respect to whom the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151. For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of section 1 a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a surviving spouse- (A) if the taxpayer has remarried at any time before the close of the taxable year, or (B) unless, for the taxpayer's taxable year during which his spouse died, a joint return could have been made. A husband and wife may make a single return jointly of income taxes, even though one of the spouses has neither gross income nor deductions, except that no joint return shall be made if either the husband or wife at any time during the taxable year is a nonresident alien.

An individual shall be considered a head of a household if, and only if, such individual is not married at the close of his taxable year, is not a surviving spouse (as defined in subsection (a)), and either- (A) maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of such taxable year the principal place of abode, as a member of such household, of- (i) a qualifying child of the individual (as defined in section 152(c)), but not if such child- (I) is married at the close of the taxpayer's taxable year, and (II) is not a dependent of such individual by reason of section 152(b)(2) or (ii) any other person who is a dependent of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such person under section 151, or (B) maintains a household which constitutes for such taxable year the principal place of abode of the father or mother of the taxpayer, if the taxpayer is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year for such father or mother under section 151. For purposes of this paragraph, an individual shall be considered as maintaining a household only if over half of the cost of maintaining the household during the taxable year is furnished by such individual. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), (A) an individual who is legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married; (B) a taxpayer shall be considered as not married at the close of his taxable year if at any time during the taxable year his spouse is a nonresident alien; and (C) a taxpayer shall be considered as married at the close of his taxable year if his spouse (other than a spouse described in subparagraph (B)) died during the taxable year. ... Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for purposes of this subtitle a taxpayer shall not be considered to be a head of a household- (A) if at any time during the taxable year he is a nonresident alien; or (B) by reason of an individual who would not be a dependent for the taxable year but for subparagraph (H) of section 152(d)(2). ... the determination of whether an individual is married shall be made as of the close of his taxable year; except that if his spouse dies during his taxable year such determination shall be made as of the time of such death; and ... an individual legally separated from his spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance shall not be considered as married. ... an individual who is married (within the meaning of subsection (a)) and who files a separate return maintains as his home a household which constitutes for more than one-half of the taxable year the principal place of abode of a child with respect to whom such individual is entitled to a deduction for the taxable year under section 151, ... such individual furnishes over one-half of the cost of maintaining such household during the taxable year, and ... during the last 6 months of the taxable year, such individual's spouse is not a member of such household, ... such individual shall not be considered as married.

sections.note: Names the four outcomes. Neither is the fallback when no other outcome's rule applies. The order (surviving spouse before head of household) also carries 3.1's 'is not a surviving spouse'.
Sets the unknowns outcome: a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to review.
Heading only; its content is in 2.1 and 2.2.
The limitations are folded into the surviving-spouse rule as required conditions: no remarriage, and no nonresident alien in the year of death, so that a joint return could have been made.
Heading only; its content is in 3.1 to 3.3.
'Is not a surviving spouse' is enforced by the outcome order, not inside the rule. The father-or-mother branch relies on abode_household_maintained_by_taxpayer for the over-half-cost test.

(C) is applied as making the taxpayer married whenever the spouse died during the year and was not a nonresident alien. This lets (C) override (A) and section 5. The SOP gives no priority among (A), (B) and (C), so a person should decide that precedence.
(B) is applied to the 'any other person who is a dependent' branch. A qualifying child or a parent cannot be a dependent only by reason of 152(d)(2)(H).
Heading only; its content is in 4.1 and 4.2.
Carried by the fact married_at_determination_date, which is already defined at the close of the year or at the spouse's death.

Lead-in: 'For purposes of those provisions of this title which refer to this subsection'. No provision in this SOP expressly refers to 7703(b). Its not-married rule (5.1 to 5.4) is nonetheless applied to 3.1's marital test. A person should confirm that section 5 is meant to apply.
